# Standalone dashboards (generated)

**Do not edit the JSON files in this directory.** They are generated from the chart dashboards in
`charts/<chart>/dashboards/` by `build.py`, and the release workflow regenerates and commits them on every release,
so any hand edit here is overwritten. To change a dashboard, edit the chart's copy and bump that chart's version.

What `build.py` changes for a standalone import: the chart-only placeholders become dashboard variables (SLO period,
probe job), the cost panels are fixed to US dollars, each file gets its own uid (so importing one never clashes with a
dashboard a chart provisioned), and `__requires` lists Grafana, Prometheus and the panel types. Run it locally with
`python3 dashboards/build.py`. A new placeholder in a chart dashboard that `build.py` does not know about fails the
build, and with it the pull-request check.

| Chart dashboard | Generated file |
|---|---|
| `charts/slo-burn-rate-alerts/dashboards/slo-overview.json` | `slo-burn-rate-error-budget.json` |
| `charts/blackbox-slo-probes/dashboards/probes.json` | `synthetic-probes-slo.json` |
| `charts/otel-collector-baseline/dashboards/otel-collector.json` | `opentelemetry-collector-agent-gateway.json` |
| `charts/k8s-cost-waste-alerts/dashboards/cost-waste.json` | `kubernetes-cost-waste-savings.json` |

Upload: grafana.com → My Account → Dashboards → Upload dashboard, one JSON at a time, then paste the summary and the
description below (the description field takes Markdown). Add the screenshot from the dev-stack Grafana. On a new
version of a dashboard, use "Upload new revision" on the existing listing rather than a new upload, so the ID and the
download count stay.

Tested 27 Oct 2026 against the dev-stack: all four import through the Grafana import API, and every panel query of
the SLO, probe and cost dashboards returns data (the OpenTelemetry traffic panels need collectors receiving data).

---

## 1. `slo-burn-rate-error-budget.json`

**Name:** SLO burn rate and error budget (Prometheus, multi-window)

**Summary:** SLI, error budget remaining and multi-window burn rates for Prometheus SLOs, with every SLO in one table.

**Description:**

```markdown
One dashboard for every SLO in your Prometheus: the SLI over the SLO period, error budget remaining and spent, burn rate over 5m to 3d windows, how long the budget lasts at the current burn rate, firing burn-rate alerts and their history, and a table of all SLOs sorted by remaining budget.

**Data it needs.** The recording rules written by the [slo-burn-rate-alerts](https://github.com/oreondev/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/slo-burn-rate-alerts) Helm chart: `slo:sli_error:ratio_rate<window>`, `slo:objective:ratio`, `slo:error_budget_remaining:ratio` and friends, labelled `slo` and `service`. The chart writes them from SLOs given as Helm values or as OpenSLO v1 documents, on Prometheus Operator or Google Managed Prometheus. No operator or controller runs in the cluster.

**How it differs from the Sloth dashboards.** Same Google SRE Workbook maths (multi-window, multi-burn-rate page and ticket alerts), different source: Sloth's dashboards read Sloth's `slo:*` rules generated by its CLI or controller; this one reads the rules a plain Helm chart renders, and adds budget-lasts and alert-history panels.

**Variables.** Data source, SLO, and the SLO period (must match the chart's `sloPeriodDays`, 30d by default).

Maintained by Oreon IT. Issues and pull requests: https://github.com/oreondev/helm-charts
```

**Tags:** slo, sli, error-budget, burn-rate, sre, prometheus, alerting

## 2. `synthetic-probes-slo.json`

**Name:** Synthetic probes with SLOs (blackbox exporter, Prometheus)

**Summary:** Availability and latency SLOs for blackbox exporter probes, with TLS expiry, status codes and per-target history.

**Description:**

```markdown
Uptime checks treated as SLOs: for each probed URL, availability and latency SLIs over the SLO period, error budget remaining, probe success over time, response time by phase, HTTP status, and days until the TLS certificate expires.

**Data it needs.** Prometheus blackbox exporter metrics (`probe_success`, `probe_duration_seconds`, `probe_http_status_code`, `probe_ssl_earliest_cert_expiry`) labelled `slo_target`, plus the recording rules of the [blackbox-slo-probes](https://github.com/oreondev/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/blackbox-slo-probes) Helm chart, which turns a list of URLs into Prometheus Operator Probe objects with those labels.

**Variables.** Data source, probe job (the chart's `probe.jobName`, `blackbox-slo` by default), SLO period and target.

Maintained by Oreon IT. https://github.com/oreondev/helm-charts
```

**Tags:** blackbox, synthetic-monitoring, uptime, slo, prometheus, tls

## 3. `opentelemetry-collector-agent-gateway.json`

**Name:** OpenTelemetry Collector: agent and gateway health

**Summary:** Throughput, refusals, export failures, queue use, memory and CPU for OpenTelemetry Collector agents and gateways.

**Description:**

```markdown
Health of OpenTelemetry Collectors from their own telemetry: spans, metric points and log records received, refused, exported and failed per second; exporter queue use against capacity and requests in flight; processor drops and memory limiter refusals; batch sizes; tail-sampling policy evaluations and load-balancing exporter backends; memory, Go heap and CPU per collector pod.

Works with any collector that exposes its internal metrics to Prometheus (`otelcol_*`, with or without the `_total` suffix). Built for the agent (DaemonSet) and gateway (Deployment) layout of the [otel-collector-baseline](https://github.com/oreondev/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/otel-collector-baseline) Helm chart, which also ships the matching alerts.

**Variables.** Data source, namespace and collector pod.

Maintained by Oreon IT. https://github.com/oreondev/helm-charts
```

**Tags:** opentelemetry, otel-collector, observability, prometheus, kubernetes

---

## 4. `kubernetes-cost-waste-savings.json`

**Name:** Kubernetes cost, showback, waste and savings (Prometheus, OpenCost)

**Summary:** Cluster cost per month, cost per namespace, requests above usage, unrequested capacity and savings levers.

**Description:**

```markdown
What the cluster costs and where to cut it: monthly cost split into requested and unrequested capacity, cost per namespace for showback, CPU and memory requested above real usage priced per month, a node table with price, capacity type and how much of each node is requested, a table of savings levers (right-sizing, consolidation, spot, commitments, idle volumes and load balancers), plus PersistentVolumeClaims no pod mounts and HorizontalPodAutoscaler limits.

**Data it needs.** The recording rules of the [k8s-cost-waste-alerts](https://github.com/oreondev/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/k8s-cost-waste-alerts) Helm chart (`costwaste:*`), built on kube-state-metrics and cAdvisor. Node prices come from flat rates, an instance-type price list in values, or OpenCost.

**Currency.** Panels are in US dollars. The chart's own copy of this dashboard uses the currency set in its values.

Maintained by Oreon IT. https://github.com/oreondev/helm-charts
```

**Tags:** kubernetes, cost, finops, opencost, showback, prometheus
